label: HMV
notes: The first complete recording of the Goldberg Variations. Landowska's pioneering harpsichord revival made this a historically significant document.

label: RCA Victor
notes: Landowska's second recording, made in her home in Lakeville, Connecticut after fleeing wartime Europe.

label: Columbia Masterworks
notes: Gould's legendary debut recording. A revolutionary interpretation that stunned the musical world with its speed, clarity, and contrapuntal precision.

label: Decca
notes: Tureck's scholarly and deeply considered interpretation. She was known as the 'High Priestess of Bach'.

label: Nonesuch
notes: Galling's clean and precise recording on a two-manual harpsichord, an early Nonesuch release.

label: Seon
notes: Leonhardt's second recording, more refined and intimate than his 1965 version.

label: Columbia Masterworks
notes: Gould's famous re-recording, slower and more introspective than his 1955 version. One of the most discussed pairs of recordings in classical music history.

label: CRD
notes: Pinnock's crisp and rhythmically vital recording with the English Concert, bringing chamber music energy to the work.

label: Decca
notes: Gulda's unconventional and jazz-inflected interpretation, a unique take that divides opinion but fascinates listeners.

label: Telefunken
notes: Leonhardt's influential recording that helped establish the historically informed performance movement.

label: Melodiya
notes: Richter's live recording from Aldeburgh. A deeply personal and poetic interpretation from one of the 20th century's greatest pianists.

label: Deutsche Grammophon
notes: Weissenberg's powerful and virtuosic interpretation, a contrast to the more common lyrical approaches.

label: Supraphon
notes: Růžičková's elegant recording, one of the few made behind the Iron Curtain. A survivor of the Holocaust, her Bach carries deep emotional weight.

label: CBS Masterworks
notes: Martins' passionate recording, part of his lifelong dedication to Bach's keyboard works despite severe hand injuries.

label: Columbia Masterworks
notes: Newman's virtuosic and rhythmically vital recording, one of the first to bring a fresh energy to harpsichord Bach in the modern era.

label: Melodiya
notes: Nikolayeva's authoritative recording from the great Russian Bach tradition. She was Shostakovich's muse for the 24 Preludes and Fugues.

label: Decca
notes: Schiff's warm, lyrical approach to the Variations, recorded at the Musikverein, Vienna.

label: Erato
notes: Ross's landmark recording of the complete Bach keyboard works. Tragically, Ross died at 38, making this recording a precious document.

label: Archiv Produktion
notes: Gilbert's refined and scholarly recording for Archiv, on a Taskin harpsichord.

label: Erato
notes: Koopman's energetic and dance-inflected recording on a Ruckers harpsichord.

label: ECM
notes: Jarrett's surprising choice to record on harpsichord. The jazz pianist brings a unique rhythmic sensibility to Bach.

label: EMI Classics
notes: Tipo's crystalline and elegant recording, praised for its clarity and singing tone.

label: Opus 111
notes: Hantaï's deeply musical recording, bringing French harpsichord tradition to its finest expression in Bach.

label: Deutsche Harmonia Mundi
notes: Staier's refined and historically informed recording on a copy of a 1728 Dulcken harpsichord.

label: Decca
notes: Hogwood's historically informed recording on an original Ruckers harpsichord from 1640.

label: Arte Nova
notes: Hill's thoughtful recording, notable for its attention to ornamentation and historical style.

label: Collins Classics
notes: MacGregor's fresh and contemporary approach, bringing a modern pianist's perspective to the work.

label: Tacet
notes: Koroliov's deeply felt recording, a hidden gem among Goldberg recordings, praised for its introspective beauty.

label: Channel Classics
notes: A unique arrangement for solo violin, revealing the work's inner voices in a completely new light.

label: Hyperion
notes: Hewitt's elegant and singing Bach, recorded on a Steinway at Henry Wood Hall, London.

label: Sony Classical
notes: Perahia's Grammy-winning recording, combining technical brilliance with deep musical understanding.

label: Harmonia Mundi
notes: Egarr's vibrant and rhythmically vital recording on a Ruckers harpsichord.

label: BMG
notes: Serkin's deeply intellectual and sensitive recording, continuing the musical legacy of his father Rudolf Serkin.

label: DG
notes: Wang's youthful and technically dazzling take on the Goldberg Variations.

label: Hyperion
notes: Demidenko's commanding recording, combining Russian pianistic tradition with Bach's contrapuntal clarity.

label: Deutsche Grammophon
notes: Stadtfeld's young and energetic recording, winner of the International Bach Competition.

label: Telarc
notes: Dinnerstein's breakout recording, self-financed and recorded at her home. It became a surprise bestseller and launched her career.

label: Decca
notes: Bahrami's warm and lyrical recording, an Italian-Iranian pianist who has become a Bach specialist.

label: Mirare
notes: Zhu Xiaomei's earlier and more spontaneous recording, before her 2017 release.

label: Deutsche Grammophon
notes: Esfahani's modern approach to the harpsichord, bringing fresh energy to the Goldberg Variations.

label: Warner Classics
notes: Rana's youthful and energetic recording, showcasing her exceptional technique.

label: Erato
notes: Fray's poetic and colorful recording, praised for its singing tone and musical intelligence.

label: Opus Arte
notes: Sokolov's live recording, praised for its extraordinary clarity and emotional depth.

label: Decca
notes: Jansen's arrangement for solo violin, bringing a warm singing tone to the keyboard work.

label: Harmonia Mundi
notes: Alard's recording on a historical Silbermann harpsichord, part of his complete Bach keyboard cycle.

label: Deutsche Grammophon
notes: Trifonov's dazzling recording, bringing his legendary virtuosity and poetic depth to Bach's masterpiece.

label: Chandos
notes: Colli's refined and intellectual recording, bringing Italian pianistic elegance to the Variations.

label: Erato
notes: Rondeau's youthful and charismatic recording, from the young French harpsichordist who has brought new audiences to the instrument.

label: Chandos
notes: Bavouzet's sparkling and transparent recording, praised for its clarity and rhythmic vitality.

label: Deutsche Grammophon
notes: Lang Lang's much-anticipated recording, a bold and personal interpretation that divided critics but showcased his artistry.

label: Sony Classical
notes: Volodos' long-awaited recording, characterized by extraordinary tonal beauty and poetic depth.

label: Myrios Classics
notes: Gerstein's recording combining intellectual rigor with pianistic brilliance, on a Steinway D.

notes: Ólafsson's much-anticipated recording from the 'Icelandic Glenn Gould', praised for its clarity and modern sensibility.
